taxonomy:
## Taxonomy of grid-based logic games (from the provided rule texts only)

### A. Placement of items on cells (lights, colored/black cells, shaded cells)
Games where the main task is **choosing which cells are filled/colored/marked**.

- **Akari**: place light bulbs in white squares; illumination constraints.
- **Choco Banana**: paint some cells black; black forms rectangles/squares; white avoids rectangle/square.
- **Hitori**: mark cells black so no duplicate numbers in any row/column; black cells not touch; white connected.
- **Kurodoko**: paint cells black; numbered cells stay white; black cells not touch; all white connected.
- **Kurotto**: color cells black according to circle-number sums; circles can’t be colored.
- **LITS**: color tetromino-shaped blocks inside bold regions; similar shapes can’t touch (except corners); no 2×2+ colored.
- **Heyawake**: paint cells black within rooms; numbers count black in room; black not connect; white connectivity/room-crossing constraints.
- **Nurikabe**: shade black cells to form a continuous wall; numbered areas constrain white sizes; no 2×2 black.
- **Nurikabe** (continued from ruleset): black wall connected; white regions each have one number.
- **Nurimeizu**: shade cells to form two same-size blocks per outlined region; no touching; no 2×2 all shaded.
- **Nurimisaki**: create “Misaki” white cells vs black; each circle number counts straight white length; no 2×2+ groups connected constraints.
- **Satogaeri**: move circles so each country has exactly one circle; circles pass through required cell counts.
- **Shakashaka**: place black triangles in squares; uncovered white region must be rectangle/square; triangle counts per cell.
- **Sto-stone**: fill/settle stones in rooms; rooms’ numbers constrain continuous black counts; falling must remove empty bottom.
- **Tilepaint**: color tiles (areas) so number rules determine required black counts along diagonals/lines.
- **Usowan**: color some cells subject to adjacency count; one wrong number per bold rectangle; colored not adjacent orthogonally.
- **Yosenabe**: move circles into gray areas matching sums; empty gray can be arbitrary but at least one circle enters.

---

### B. Drawing non-self-intersecting single loops (loop/outline puzzles)
Games where the core action is **drawing one continuous loop** through cell centers/edges.

- **Dotchi-Loop**: loop through all white circles’ cells; straight-through or right-angled turn rule per enclosed area; cannot go through black circles.
- **Double Choco**: (not a loop) *excluded* from this category.
- **Mid-loop**: loop through all black circles; each black circle is midpoint of straight segment.
- **Masyu**: loop passes through all circles; black vs white circle dictate right-turn/straight behavior.
- **Nagareru**: loop forms a continuous loop following wind direction constraints from arrows in black cells.
- **Moon-or-Sun**: loop enters rooms; each room visited once; in each room loop goes through all moons or all suns (not both); adjacency room transfer moons/suns.
- **Ripple Effect**: (not loop) *excluded* from this category.
- **Suraromu**: loop passes all “gates” exactly once; starts/returns at open numbered circle; gate numbers constrain crossing order/direction.
- **Slitherlink**: loop through dots so number counts how many line segments surround each cell.
- **Yajilin**: loop drawn; numbers point to count of black cells in arrow direction; loop must not go through black/number cells; black cells can’t touch orthogonally.

---

### C. Drawing paths/lines that connect pairs or trace routes (non-loop connectivity)
Games where the core is **connecting specific endpoints** (often with no crossing/branching).

- **Hebi**: place sequential snake parts 1→5 in white cells; numbers in black squares constrain visibility to next black.
- **Hashiwokakero**: connect numbered islands with bridges; bridge count per island; bridges don’t cross islands/other bridges; all islands linked.
- **Numberlink**: connect pairs of equal numbers by continuous line; lines go orthogonally; no crossing; cannot pass through number cells.
- **Pencils**: draw pencils starting from a tip; pencil is straight chain of cells; length determined by numbers; no self-cross/branching.
- **Nansuke**: fill grid with numbers from orientation (left-to-right / up-to-down) implied by rules, not a path.
- **Norinori**: place blocks in twos in consecutive black squares (placement, not path).
- **Yajilin** already categorized under loops.

---

### D. Area partitioning into rectangles/blocks with tiling/regions
Games where the essential task is **partitioning the grid into regions/blocks/rooms**, and then applying constraints.

- **Shikaku**: divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number equal to its area size.
- **Fillomino**: partition into blocks; each block size equals the number; same-sized blocks can’t touch orthogonally.
- **Juosan**: fill grid with “—” or “|”; bold-line enclosed territories; each territory number counts extra marks; constraints on how far marks extend.
- **Nurikabe**: not a partitioning puzzle (it uses continuous wall/white regions), so excluded here.
- **Chained Block**: partition into blocks of consecutive black cells; each block has a size number/“?”; blocks touching at corners create chains; chain has no repeated block shape/size.
- **Double Choco**: divide grid into blocks by solid lines over dotted lines; blocks contain pair of same-form white/gray areas; numbers give half block cell counts.
- **Five Cells**: divide grid into blocks of five cells; numbers count lines around cells including outer frame; lines can’t enter a block.
- **LITS**: bold-line areas (not partitioning done by player) are used to constrain placement; the player colors tetrominoes inside.
- **Satogaeri**: bold-line “Countries” are pre-defined regions; player moves circles into them.
- **Suraromu**: gates and loop; regions exist only by gates/border; not a rectangle partition.
- **Sto-stone**: “Rooms” are bold-line enclosed; stone falling into bottom half constrained.
- **Ripple Effect**: rooms defined by bold lines; rooms filled with consecutive numbers starting from 1.
- **Tilepaint**: “Tiles” are bold-line enclosed; color tiles with rules.
- **Nurimeizu / Nurimisaki / Heyawake / Sashigane / Satogaeri / Sto-stone / Ripple Effect / Suraromu**: all use bold-line enclosed “rooms/regions” (pre-defined), but still primarily constrain placement or movement; they belong more naturally in A or B/C as above.

---

### E. Grid filling with numbers under arithmetic/ordering rules
Games where the core is **assigning numbers** (digits) to cells, governed by given numeric constraints.

- **Sudoku**: place 1–9 in each empty cell; each row/column/3×3 block contains all 1–9.
- **Nansuke**: fill blanks with numbers from a list; each cell has only one digit; numbers are up-down or left-to-right.
- **Ripple Effect**: fill each room with consecutive numbers starting from 1; duplication in row/column forces spacing ≥ value.
- **Fillomino**: numbers are given and used to size blocks; still a filling/propagation constraint, but mainly operates via region/block constraints (see C/D).
- **Usowan**: numbers indicate adjacent colored cells, with one wrong number per bold rectangle.
- **Chained Block**: numbers specify black-cell block sizes; “?” blocks unknown.
- **Heyawake**: room numbers constrain count of painted (black) cells.
- **Kurodoko**: numbers constrain number of white cells up to nearest black or frame.

---

### F. Connectivity/structure constraints on colored cells (without necessarily being loop/path)
Games where the key is **connectivity, separation, or non-adjacency** of colored/white/black cells.

- **Hitori**: black cells not touch; white connected.
- **Heyawake**: painted cells not connected; white can’t stretch across >2 rooms; white separated by painted cells not allowed.
- **Kurodoko**: black cells not touch orthogonally; all white connected.
- **Nurikabe**: black wall connected; no 2×2 black.
- **Nurimeizu**: two blocks in a region must not touch; no 2×2 fully shaded.
- **Nurimisaki**: white cells continuous; avoid 2×2+ links for black/white.
- **Yajilin**: black cells can’t touch orthogonally; loop doesn’t pass through black/number cells.
- **Usowan**: colored cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by colored cells.

---

### Notes on overlaps (still based only on the given rules)
- **Akari** combines cell placement with illumination-based connectivity constraints (Category A).
- **Chained Block** and **Fillomino** are both “region/block” heavy but are distinct: Chained Block’s blocks are defined by consecutive black cells and chains; Fillomino’s blocks are filled to match numbers (Category D + A/B depending on view, but listed under D/structure emphasis).
- **Loop vs non-loop** is separated: any puzzle where the rules explicitly say *draw a single loop* goes under Category B.
